what: When any part of this element (usually the footer) enters the screen, the black contrast-stage panel behind the page slowly covers it with 2s cubic-bezier(.55,.08,.68,.53) (easeInQuad), and <body> When .is-fx-night is added, the text on the writing side turns white — when you leave, the panel lifts over 1s cubic-bezier(.39,.57,.56,1) (easeOutSine). A pastel-sky page turns to night at the end

options.z: Panel z-index, default -1 (behind body, in front of fixed background)
options.--fx-night: Panel color (CSS variable, <body> In ), default var(--kf-contrast-bg)
options.line: Night (0–100) only while the section spans a line at some % from the top of the screen — not when any part is visible, but while it passes that horizontal line (example 50: while the section spans the screen’s middle line)

use: <footer data-fx="night-fall-cover">…</footer>  /* Writing-side css: body.is-fx-night { color: var(--kf-contrast-ink) } */
note: The board <body> Create only one at the end (even if the same part is attached to several elements there is one panel — if any one is visible, it is night). Changing text color differs per site, so the user’s css does it with .is-fx-night

from.where: index.html footer — original $('#footer').on('inview') → #home.color-white · #bg-black.visible(opacity 2s easeInQuad) / hidden(1s easeOutSine)

shared.js [data-bg=pic] — the original ly_bg blurred denim photo spreads in over .8s (power1.out) while the section crosses the screen’s center line (top 50% to bottom 50%), and the text and dotted lines turn cream → line: 50; in: .8; out: .8; ease-in·ease-out: cubic-bezier(.25,.46,.45,.94), photo in --fx-night (url() center / cover)
